text:
The Voskresen manuscript was written in Middle Low German, according to a linguistic analysis released on 14 March 2024 by the Institute for Northern Codicology.

The finding appears in the Institute's peer-reviewed report "Language and Provenance of the Voskresen Codex" (Report No. 7), which draws on a survey of the manuscript carried out in 2023. Of the codex's 212 vellum leaves, 187 were confirmed as Middle Low German in both script and vocabulary, the report states.

Dr. Halvard Teskemar, the Institute's lead palaeographer, directed the study. The report bases its conclusion on the language of the text and the letterforms used by the scribes, rather than on the manuscript's later history of ownership.

The report does not attribute a language to the remaining 25 leaves in the passage reviewed by this newspaper. The Institute describes Report No. 7 as its formal account of the codex's language and origins.
